issues.body: Recovery 2 says an operator may add an enrolled handle in an ordinary policy PR and then edit the account issue's `grant_targets:` line. But `grant_targets:` is generated from live `grant:` labels; editing it after the fact does not prove that the request ever authorized the new target. An ordinary policy PR also does not establish the row-scoped `account-pool/<handle>` provenance that the broker and no-op activation path explicitly require. Since claim selection reads `account_pool` and does not validate `grant_targets:`, the policy half takes effect immediately, so calling the editable record "the authorization record" is materially misleading and the proposed two-step window is not fail-closed.
issues.fix_hint: Document widening through an authorization flow that reuses/rechecks audited `grant:<owner>/<repo>` labels and lands the addition through the checked `account-pool/<handle>` path, then updates the record from that proven target set. If manual policy changes are intentionally a separate authorization mechanism, state that explicitly and do not characterize a hand-edited issue line as proof of the original broker authorization.
issues.title: Manual grant widening bypasses the documented authorization and provenance controls

issues.body: Recovery 1 describes an unmerged pending `account-pool/<handle>` PR and then says to "merge the pending PR (or re-run `activate` on it ...)". The workflow's `activate` job is gated on `pull_request.merged == true`; re-running it on an unmerged PR remains skipped and cannot recover the account.
issues.fix_hint: Say to merge the corrected pending PR, or re-run the activation workflow/job only after the PR has merged; retain re-applying `set-up-account` as the pre-merge resume option.
issues.title: Recovery suggests activation can be re-run before the pending PR merges

verdict.summary: The new recovery guidance conflates a broker-generated activation proof with the authorization source and recommends a widening procedure that bypasses the broker's live grant-label check and checked grant-PR provenance. That is unsafe guidance for this trust boundary. There is also a smaller inaccurate recovery instruction about re-running activation on an unmerged pending PR.
